### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/cli`, `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **81** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/mapping.md`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**67** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e`.

⛔ **19** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts`, `packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json`, `packages/spec/liveness/state-counts/mapping.md`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `isSystem (5 routes)`
- **2** anchor(s) matched too much of the corpus to be a work list: `created_at (literal, 43 pages)`, `organization_id (literal, 40 pages)`
- **34** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **181** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `e1173802f6be68f63a462d73d77d4cf54fba6cb2` — the merge of head `de2dd9b002254c576642b64f83dd45ad0dec3bfc` into base `26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin e1173802f6be68f63a462d73d77d4cf54fba6cb2 && git checkout e1173802f6be68f63a462d73d77d4cf54fba6cb2
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e de2dd9b002254c576642b64f83dd45ad0dec3bfc && git checkout -B drift-repro 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e && git merge --no-ff de2dd9b002254c576642b64f83dd45ad0dec3bfc

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 26f4e6d84af886706501e759b9385673615ee39e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `a87604acfccb96ac1eef0d96dc30ddd76967841c`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-sync-run.object.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-run-ledger.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/pull-refusal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts, packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json

Rendered 2026-11-11T03:52Z by an isolated read-only subagent. Inputs: card #32062 (body and all 14 comments), PR #32385 (body, 21-file list, net diff against `main` at merge base `d48fb153`), the check-runs on the head, ADR-0153 and the cited code read in the tree. The rest of the diff (tests, censuses, the CLI inventory row, ledgers, `jobs.mdx`, both changesets' prose beyond ②) is the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT` and is not reviewed here.

Check-runs on the head: 57 success, 10 skipped, 1 failure. The failure is `Check Changeset`, step "Reject an empty-frontmatter changeset added by this PR", the foreign-changeset rule's DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, red by design; ② judges it.

### ① Derived judgments

1. `PLATFORM_OBJECTS_BY_PACKAGE['service-automation']` gains `sys_sync_run`, so `PLATFORM_PROVIDED_OBJECT_NAMES` and `isPlatformProvidedObjectName('sys_sync_run')` now answer true. A widening: a stack reference to that name moves from "no known package registers this" to resolved. **Right.** The group stays "the exact set that package registers": `plugin.ts` registers `SysSyncRun` on both paths (`registerRunObject`, and `registerCredentialObject` under `suspendedRunStore: 'memory'`), and the owning package's pin (`activation-ledger-registration.test.ts`) names the sixth object. No other group or export of the file moves.
2. A new platform object with `apiMethods: ['get', 'list']`: a new read surface on the data API, no write surface. Widening. **Right**, and it follows `sys_automation_run`.
3. `ConnectorPullRefusalReason` gains `run_record_unavailable` (503). An additive member of an exported union, and a new refusal on a path that ran before: a connector pull is now refused when the run row cannot be opened, although a connector source reads no position from it. **Right as declared**: it is stated in the changeset, a composition with no ledger still runs, and ADR-0153 D4's `_sync_run_id` makes the run row load-bearing for both sources.
4. `datasourceSource.full` flips `planned` to `live` and loses `authorWarn`; the `watermark.start` and container rows are reworded. **Right**: `pullDatasourceSource` reads `ds.full === true` to skip `run.lastCommitted()`, and the evidence anchor names that function.
5. `@objectstack/service-automation` exports `SysSyncRun`, the ledger, `closeInterruptedSyncRuns`, two constants and eight types; `ConnectorPullDeps.runs` is optional. Additive. **Right.** `pullDatasourceSource` gains a required fourth parameter, but it is not exported from the package root.
6. A datasource pull's starting point changes from `watermark.start` to the committed position. The behaviour it replaces is slice 2's, unreleased and in the same release. **Right as a widening**, subject to S1 below on what "the mapping" is.
7. Card #32062 declares `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` for the whole card (D8, D3). This slice carries neither, and its own line is `yes (widening)`. **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/32062-sync-in-run-record.md`: `minor` for `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/cli`. It matches what the diff publishes: a new exported surface and object in service-automation, one added name in a spec constant, an inventory row in the CLI (spec and cli are in the fixed group). No major is implied: nothing released is removed or narrowed.
- Clause-②: `yes (widening)` on the PR body and on the changeset, with `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. Correct for this diff: no authorable key is added, removed or narrowed, and one key (`full`) gains its reader.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION, confirmed by this record on this head.** The one pending note modified is `.changeset/32062-sync-in-datasource-pull.md` (slice 2, #32339, unreleased). Sentence by sentence:
  - Before: "**No committed position is kept yet.** The read position is stored on `sys_sync_run` (ADR-0153 D7), which lands separately. Until then every run reads from `watermark.start`, so an incremental pull reads what a `full` one reads. The keyed upsert keeps the rows right, but every run rewrites every row of the `synced` target: record-triggered automations run, audit rows are written and `updated_at` moves for each row, on every run, until the slice that stores the read position lands. `datasourceSource.full`, `deletePolicy` and `deletedField` still warn their author that they change nothing yet." This head makes every sentence of it false except the last, and the last is false for `full`.
  - After, sentence 1: "Each run reads on from the read position the last run of the mapping committed, stored on `sys_sync_run` (ADR-0153 D7, in the same release: see its own entry), so it reads only the rows written since, plus the rows sharing that position, which the keyed upsert writes again harmlessly." True against `datasource-pull.ts` (`from = Math.max(reading.canon, start)`, windows read from `from` inclusive). It leaves out "in the same organization, on the same source object and field", which the entry it points to carries. Accepted. S1 applies to this sentence as it does to the new entry.
  - After, sentence 2: "The first run, and every run of a mapping that declares `full: true`, reads from `watermark.start`." True (`previous` is `undefined` on both).
  - After, sentence 3: "`deletePolicy` and `deletedField` still warn their author that they change nothing yet." True against `packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json` on this head.
  - The correction is a correction, not a collision. Restoring the base text would publish a false note beside the new entry in one release.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Open question (report 6784859606): `job_run_id` and the trigger are not recorded, though D7 lists both and D8 names `sys_sync_run.job_run_id`.** Answered, not escalated: it is staging inside an open card, disclosed on the object's doc, the changeset and the PR body, and the two columns are additive. Option A is consistent with seat answer 1 of 6773389044 (a `contracts/` hunk may ride a product PR, declared `Clause-②: yes`, owing its own review at this tier). The choice between A and B stays the seat's; it is not a maintainer fork, since the ADR already names the column. The card must not close without the two columns or a dated ADR note.
- **Deviation: the one `packages/spec/src` hunk.** The claim forbids other spec hunks; this one is forced by the file's own maintenance contract. Right, and it is the `hits` file.
- **Deviation: the run is scoped by the organization its row stores.** Read in `sync-run-ledger.ts#open` and `connector-pull.ts#openSyncRun`: both later reads and the hand-over use the stored value. Holds.
- **Deviation: the `committed_at` guard has no test of its own.** Read by hand: step 1 sets the row's own flag, step 2 clears only rows with an earlier `committed_at`, so every ordering of two runs' four writes leaves at least the later one flagged, and `lastCommitted` orders by the same column. Holds. Clock skew between replicas can leave two holders, never none.
- **Not recorded yet: marked-deleted and `skipped_null_watermark` counts.** Staged with D3, disclosed. Accepted.
- **Out of scope, carried:** the stale "READ BY NOTHING YET" JSDoc in `packages/spec/src/data/mapping.zod.ts` keeps its carrier (the next slice touching the file).
- **Observation for the D8 slice, no finding:** under a walled posture a pull in no organization opens a row with `organization_id` NULL. Whether the engine accepts that insert was not read here. D8's boot and door refusals remove the case.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` (hits).** The hunk holds against its contract and its first consumers. The name is real on every composition that registers anything (both manifest paths), the list stays sorted, the JSDoc names what the object is, and the conformance pin in the owning package moved with it. `dangling-reference-audit.ts` reads only the `plugin-security` group; `stack.zod.ts` uses its own prefix predicate. No finding.

**The implementing files, against ADR-0153 D7, invariants 8 and 9, and the code on `main`.**

Holds, read in the tree:
- The position round-trips: `spellCanon` writes an ISO date-time, an ISO date or an integer, the ledger stores `String(position)`, and `canonOf` reads each back (an integer from its decimal text).
- `$null` is in the filter grammar (`filter.zod.ts`), so `watermark_committed: { $null: false }` and the no-organization scope are real predicates.
- Invariant 8: `commit` is the window reader's hook, called at a window's end only; a failed commit throws `run_record_unavailable` before the next window is read.
- Retention: `onlyWhen` matches only ended rows with `holds_position: false`; `open` writes `false` explicitly, so no row is NULL there. The latest committed row of a scope is always a holder.
- The failure text: every `ConnectorPullError` sentence is platform-authored; a foreign error is reduced to its code.
- The boot close sits after the suspended-run wiring in `start()`, where the sibling stores already read their tables, and a failure is caught and logged.

Findings:

- **S1 (should-fix) — the read position is keyed by the bare mapping name, but a mapping is addressed by `(package, name)`, and the target is not part of the key.** `SyncRunScope` is `{ mapping, organizationId }` with `mapping = opts.mapping`; the row stores neither the package that holds the mapping nor `targetObject`; `pullDatasourceSource` accepts a stored position when `source` and `watermark_field` match. On this same head `pullOnce` resolves the mapping through `mappingByPackage(name, callerPackageId)` (ADR-0150 D3, #32294), so two packages, or a package and the environment's own mapping, may each hold a mapping of one name and be pulled in one organization. Two breaks, both silent, both with a `completed` run:
  1. *Two mappings of one name.* If they read different sources, each run's `lastCommitted` finds the other's row, the guard fails, and both read from `watermark.start` on every run: the cost this slice says it ends, with a start line that says only `watermark.start`. If they read the same federated object on the same field into different targets, the second mapping's first run starts at the first one's position and its target never receives the history.
  2. *One mapping whose `targetObject` is edited.* The next run resumes from the old target's position; the new target holds only rows written since.
  The contract sentences this PR publishes ("the next pull of the mapping in the same organization starts there", in the object's doc, `jobs.mdx`, the changeset and the liveness note) are false in both cases. Remedy: store the holding package (the resolved holder, not the caller) and the target object on the row, scope `lastCommitted` and the hand-over by the package, and add the target to the same-source guard; one test for each break. Both columns are additive. This is the same class as slice 1's S1 (a position defect that can pass rows) and is graded as that one was: it must land, with a delta review, before any release carries `.changeset/32062-sync-in-run-record.md`. It does not block this head, because nothing here is released and the card stays open.
- **N1 (nit) — the boot close closes a run that is live on another replica.** `closeInterruptedSyncRuns` matches every `running` row; a rolling restart shows a live pull as `failed` / `interrupted` until its own close rewrites it. Disclosed in the PR body and the JSDoc, and no position is read by status. Accepted deviation; a follow-up card if run history gains readers that act on status.
- **N2 (nit, prose) — `run_record_unavailable` is described as two cases, and the code has four.** The changeset and the `pull-refusal.ts` JSDoc name the open and the commit. `openSyncRun` also raises it when `describe` fails and when `lastCommitted` cannot be read. The `describe` sentence says "the windows finished before stay written" on a path where none was read.
- **N3 (nit, comment) — `organization_id`'s comment says the column is empty for "a `single` posture job that declares and derives none".** Under `single` the engine stamps the Default Organization, which is the reason `open` reads the row back. The comment and the ledger's own doc disagree.
- **N4 (nit) — a stored position that is not used leaves no trace.** When the source or field guard fails, or `canonOf` cannot read the stored text, the run starts at `watermark.start` and the start line gives no reason. One clause in that line would have made S1's first break visible.
- **N5 (nit) — reads follow the wildcard grant.** D7 says the organization's administrators read run history; `get` / `list` are open as on `sys_automation_run`. The row holds no secret. For the P3 Studio child to settle.
- **N6 (nit) — `SyncRunOpened` is not exported from the package root, though `SyncRunLedger.open` returns it.** A host that writes its own ledger cannot name the type. Under `suspendedRunStore: 'memory'` a manifest that arrives only at `start()` is not retried for this object; the one warn line covers it.

Nits are fixed on prose faces only, or left as accepted deviations; none moves this verdict. S1 earns a delta review of its fix.

Reviewed-by: `session_01QSeKYm8sWjp2Pk76warN7w` (contract-review subagent, isolated from the dispatch; container id `cse_01QSeKYm8sWjp2Pk76warN7w`)

**VERDICT: PASS**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `de2dd9b002254c576642b64f83dd45ad0dec3bfc`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/sys-sync-run.object.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/sync-run-ledger.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/connector-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/datasource-pull.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/pull-refusal.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/plugin.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/index.ts, packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json

Delta review, rendered 2026-11-11T04:56Z by the same isolated read-only subagent as record 6786503520 (head `a87604ac`). Inputs: card #32062 with every comment through the dev's addendum 6787397120, PR #32385's body and file list, the net diff `a87604ac..de2dd9b0` (10 files, +311 / −56), the full diff against `main` for context, and the check-runs on this head. The cited code (`package-scoped-resolution.ts`, `protocol-meta-item-reads.ts`) was read, not reviewed. Tests, `jobs.mdx` and the changesets' prose beyond ② stay the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`.

Check-runs on the head: 57 success, 10 skipped, 1 failure. The failure is `Check Changeset`, the DELIBERATE CORRECTION class, red by design; ② judges it again because the corrected note moved.

### ① Derived judgments

The seven judgments of 6786503520 stand on this head; the hits file and `plugin.ts` are unchanged by the delta. What the delta adds:

1. `sys_sync_run` gains two optional read-only text columns, `mapping_package` and `target_object`, and its first index gains `mapping_package`. Additive on an object no release has carried. **Right.**
2. `SyncRunScope`, `SyncRunDescription` and `SyncRunPosition` (exported types) each gain an optional member. Additive. **Right.** `SyncRunHandle` gains `identify` and `targetObject`, and `SyncRunMappingIdentity` is new; neither is exported from the package root.
3. The resume rule narrows inside this PR's own unreleased behaviour: a stored position is now used only by the same holder package, name, organization, source object, field and target. Every case it stops resuming starts at `watermark.start`, the safe side. **Right**, and judgment 6 of the first record now holds without a qualifier.

### ② Semver level

- `.changeset/32062-sync-in-run-record.md` stays `minor` for `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec` and `@objectstack/cli`. Still right: the delta adds columns and optional type members only.
- Clause-②: `yes (widening)`, `Metadata-protocol: semantic`, on the PR body and the changeset. Still right.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION, confirmed by this record on this head.** The one pending note modified is `.changeset/32062-sync-in-datasource-pull.md` (slice 2, #32339, unreleased). The base text is the one quoted in 6786503520 ("**No committed position is kept yet.** …"), false on this head for the reasons given there. The note now reads, sentence by sentence:
  - "Each run reads on from the read position the last run of the same mapping (its package and name) committed in the same organization, stored on `sys_sync_run` (ADR-0153 D7, in the same release: see its own entry), so it reads only the rows written since, plus the rows sharing that position, which the keyed upsert writes again harmlessly." True against `scopeWhere` (holder package, name, organization) and `from = Math.max(reading.canon, start)`.
  - "The first run, every run of a mapping that declares `full: true`, and a run whose mapping now reads another source object or field or writes another target, read from `watermark.start`." True against the guard `sameRead && previous.targetObject === targetObject` and `ds.full === true`.
  - "`deletePolicy` and `deletedField` still warn their author that they change nothing yet." True against `packages/spec/liveness/mapping.json` on this head.
  - **The PR body's quote of this note is the previous head's wording.** The gate's remedy asks for the corrected sentences quoted on the PR. The seat rewrites the body's quote to the three sentences above before the queue; this is prose and does not move the head.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **PR body, stale in the places the dev lists in 6787397120** (the run-record bullet, the committed-position bullet, the retention bullet, the `run_record_unavailable` bullet's three places, Tests and Verification, and the DELIBERATE CORRECTION quote). The dev cannot edit the body. The seat rewrites it; ④ judged the tree, not the body.
- **Migration: no real concern.** No release has carried `sys_sync_run`. A row written by the previous head's code has both new columns NULL. For a packaged mapping it falls outside the new scope; for an environment mapping it is in scope but fails the target guard. Both start once from `watermark.start`, which re-reads and never skips. Such a row can keep `holds_position` true with no later run to clear it, on development databases only.
- The open question on `job_run_id` and the trigger, the accepted deviations and the D8 observation of 6786503520 are unchanged.

### ④ Design judgment

**`packages/spec/src/system/constants/platform-object-names.ts` (hits).** Unchanged by the delta; the first record's judgment stands. No finding.

**S1 — FIXED.** Read in the tree:
- *The key.* `scopeWhere` is `{ mapping, mapping_package (or $null), organization_id (or $null) }`, and both `lastCommitted` and the hand-over's clearing update use it. The hand-over therefore never clears another package's holder.
- *The holder, not the caller.* On a package read, `packageOfHolder(byPackage.holder)` takes the resolved holder (`kind: 'package'`); the environment and platform kinds key as no package. On a no-package read, `servedHolderPackage` takes the answer's `packageId` and drops the two values core does not read as a package (`sys_metadata`, `__runtime__`).
- *The target.* `describe` stores `target_object`, `lastCommitted` returns it, and the guard requires it equal. `describe` runs before the first commit on the datasource path, so every row that holds a position also holds its identity.
- *The three breaks.* Two packages with different sources: pinned by case 1 (two positions, two holders). Same source into two targets: case 3. An edited `targetObject`: case 4. Cases 2 and 5 pin holder-not-caller and the marker rule.
- *The ablations.* They cover each new key part: the package scope (case 1), the target guard (case 4), holder versus caller (case 2), the markers (case 5), and both parts off together (cases 1, 3 and 4). The dev's explanation of case 3, that either part alone holds it, matches the code.

Attempts to break the new keying, none of which succeeded:
- *A holder that is not resolved.* A package read that resolves nothing leaves `artifact` undefined and is refused `mapping_not_found` before `identify`; the row holds no position. With no `mappingByPackage` resolver, the read falls to the no-package path and keys by the served package.
- *One mapping reached by two routes that key differently* (for example a packaged mapping served under a marker on the no-package route). It splits into two positions; each route resumes its own, and neither skips a row.
- *Two mappings that collapse into one key.* The guard then still requires the same source object, field and target, and for a run writing the same target from the same source the shared position is the right one.
- *A target changed and changed back.* The latest committed row names the other target, so the run starts at `watermark.start`.
- *Rows from the previous head.* See ③: safe side.

Every mis-keying I could construct ends in a re-read from `watermark.start`, never a skipped row.

**N2 — FIXED.** `pull-refusal.ts` and the changeset name the four places. The `describe` and last-position sentences end "Nothing was read."; only the commit sentence says the earlier windows stay written.

**N3 — FIXED.** The `organization_id` comment now says the engine stamps the Default Organization under `single` and that this is why the ledger reads the stored value back.

**Carried forward as accepted, unchanged:** N1 (the boot close also closes a run live on another replica), N4 (a stored position that is not used leaves no reason in the start line; it now also covers a target mismatch), N5 (reads follow the wildcard grant; for the P3 Studio child), N6 (`SyncRunOpened` not exported from the package root; no late-manifest retry under `suspendedRunStore: 'memory'`).

**New in the delta:**
